slides.1.title: Alentejo: Regional Character
slides.1.html:
Alentejo is a vast plain in southern Portugal, covering about one third of the country, and is one of its largest wine regions.

🌡️ Climate

  • A mix of Mediterranean and continental influences
  • Long, scorching summers with temperatures that can exceed 40°C
  • More than 3,000 hours of sunshine a year
  • Low rainfall (400–600mm/year) with a distinct dry season

🪨 Soils

  • Mainly granite and gneiss (plutonic rocks)
  • Some areas have schist (xistos) and limestone (calcário)
  • Fertile land is mostly used for farming and pasture, while vines are planted on poorer ground

🍇 Main Varieties

  • Red: Aragonez (= Tempranillo) · Trincadeira · Alicante Bouschet
  • White: Antão Vaz · Arinto · Roupeiro

🗺️ The 8 Sub-regions

Portalegre · Borba · Redondo · Reguengos · Vidigueira · Évora · Granja-Amareleja · Moura
slides.2.question: What is Alentejo's most important red grape, "Aragonez", called in Spain?
slides.2.explanation: Aragonez is Alentejo's most important red variety and is the Portuguese name for Spain's famous Tempranillo. In the Douro the same variety is called Tinta Roriz.
